title: The President
note: Drafted for Prompt 12 (Unit 2). Every lesson is a draft until a person reviews it (content/course/README.md).

listen.explanationKey: The President of the United States is elected for how many years?
facts: Americans elect a President every four years.
A President can serve only two terms. This rule is in the 22nd Amendment.
The two terms do not have to be back to back. A President can serve one term, lose an election, and win again later. That is still two terms.
The rule keeps a president from becoming too powerful.

newWords.meaning: the number of years a person serves in a job
a change or addition to the Constitution
the amendment that limits a President to two terms

story.say: Americans elect a President every four years.

help.simpler: Every four years, people vote for President.
help.example: There was a presidential election in 2024. The next one is in 2028.
help.why: The test asks how many years a President is elected for. The answer is four.

check.statement: The President is elected for six years.

story.say: A President can serve only two terms.

help.simpler: One person can be President for two terms at most. That is eight years.
help.example: A President who has won two elections cannot run a third time.
help.why: The test asks why a President can serve only two terms.

story.say: This rule is in the 22nd Amendment.

help.simpler: The two-term rule was added to the Constitution as the 22nd Amendment.
help.example: Franklin Roosevelt was elected four times. After that, the 22nd Amendment set the limit.
help.why: “Because of the 22nd Amendment” is one answer on the test.

check.prompt: Tap the term that is not allowed.

story.say: The two terms do not have to be back to back.

help.simpler: A President can serve one term, stop, and later serve a second term.
help.example: Grover Cleveland served one term, lost, and then won again four years later.
help.why: Either way, the limit is still two terms.

story.say: A President can serve one term, lose an election, and win again later. That is still two terms.

help.simpler: Losing in between does not reset the count. Two terms is the most.
help.example: Term 1, then a break, then Term 2. There is no Term 3.
help.why: This helps you understand the two-term rule clearly.

check.prompt: How many terms can a President serve?

story.say: The rule keeps a president from becoming too powerful.

help.simpler: If one person led for too long, they could gain too much power.
help.example: A limit makes sure new leaders come in over time.
help.why: “To keep the president from becoming too powerful” is the other answer on the test.

readIt.sentence: When do we vote for President?

writeIt.sentence: We vote for President in November.

listen.explanationKey: Name one power of the president.
facts: The President signs bills into law and can veto bills.
The President is the Commander in Chief of the military.
The President also appoints federal judges.

newWords.meaning: the leader of all the armed forces

story.say: The President has important powers.

help.simpler: The Constitution gives the President certain jobs.
help.example: Four of them are in the picture.
help.why: The test asks you to name one power of the President.

story.say: The President signs bills into law and can veto bills.

help.simpler: The President says yes to a bill by signing it, or no by vetoing it.
help.example: Congress sends a bill. The President signs it, and it becomes a law.
help.why: “Signs bills into law” and “Vetoes bills” are both answers for a power of the President.

story.say: The President is the Commander in Chief of the military.

help.simpler: The President is the top leader of the U.S. military.
help.example: The Army, Navy, Air Force and Marines all answer to the President.
help.why: The test asks who is Commander in Chief. The answer is the President.

check.prompt: Tap the power that leads the military.

story.say: The President also appoints federal judges.

help.simpler: The President chooses people to be federal judges.
help.example: The Senate must also agree before a judge takes the job.
help.why: “Appoints federal judges” is another power of the President on the test.

check.prompt: Who is Commander in Chief of the U.S. military?

readIt.sentence: Who lives in the White House?

writeIt.sentence: The President lives in the White House.

listen.explanationKey: Why is the Electoral College important?
facts: The Electoral College decides who is elected President.
When you vote for President, you are really choosing your state's electors. Electors are people who vote for President for their state.
Each state gets as many electors as it has members of Congress: its two senators plus its representatives. Washington, D.C. gets 3. There are 538 electors in all.
In most states, the candidate who gets the most votes wins all of that state's electors. To become President, a candidate needs 270 electoral votes.
The Electoral College is a compromise between a vote of the people and a choice by Congress.

newWords.meaning: a person chosen to vote for President for a state
an agreement where each side gets part of what it wants

story.say: The Electoral College decides who is elected President.

help.simpler: A group called the Electoral College chooses the President.
help.example: It is not a school. Here, “college” means a group of people.
help.why: The test asks why the Electoral College is important. “It decides who is elected president” is one answer.

story.say: When you vote for President, you are really choosing your state’s electors.

help.simpler: Your vote helps pick your state’s electors.
help.example: If most people in your state vote for one candidate, that candidate’s electors usually win.
help.why: This explains how a citizen’s vote counts for President.

story.say: Electors are people who vote for President for their state.

help.simpler: Electors cast the official votes for President.
help.example: After the election in November, the electors meet and vote in December.
help.why: The word “elector” helps you understand the Electoral College.

check.prompt: What decides who is elected President?

story.say: Each state gets as many electors as its members of Congress: two senators plus its representatives.

help.simpler: A state’s electors = its senators + its representatives.
help.example: A state with 2 senators and 8 representatives has 10 electors.
help.why: This is why bigger states have more electors.

story.say: Washington, D.C. gets 3. There are 538 electors in all.

help.simpler: D.C. is not a state, but it gets 3 electors.
help.example: 435 representatives + 100 senators + 3 for D.C. = 538.
help.why: Knowing 538 helps you understand the number needed to win.

story.say: In most states, the candidate with the most votes wins all of that state’s electors.

help.simpler: In most states, the winner takes all the electors.
help.example: Two states, Maine and Nebraska, can split their electors.
help.why: This is why candidates try to win whole states.

story.say: To become President, a candidate needs 270 electoral votes.

help.simpler: A candidate needs 270 of the 538 votes. That is more than half.
help.example: 270 is just over half of 538.
help.why: The candidate with 270 or more electoral votes becomes President.

story.say: The Electoral College is a compromise between a vote of the people and a choice by Congress.

help.simpler: The writers of the Constitution mixed two ideas: a vote of the people and a choice by Congress.
help.example: Some wanted the people to choose. Others wanted Congress to choose. This was the middle way.
help.why: This compromise is the other answer on the test about the Electoral College.

listen.explanationKey: If the president can no longer serve, who becomes president?
facts: If the President dies or can no longer do the job, the Vice President becomes President.

newWords.meaning: the person who becomes President if the President can no longer serve

story.say: Sometimes a President cannot finish the job.

help.simpler: A President might die, or become too sick to do the job.
help.example: This has happened several times in American history.
help.why: The country always needs a President, so there is a plan.

story.say: If the President dies or can no longer do the job, the Vice President becomes President.

help.simpler: If the President cannot do the job, the Vice President takes over.
help.example: In 1963, President Kennedy died. Vice President Johnson became President that same day.
help.why: The test asks who becomes President if the President can no longer serve. The answer is the Vice President.

check.prompt: Who becomes President if the President can no longer serve? Tap them.

story.say: This way, the country always has a President.

help.simpler: The change happens right away, so the job is never empty.
help.example: The new President takes the oath of office, often on the same day.
help.why: This rule keeps the government working.

check.prompt: If the President can no longer serve, who becomes President?

listen.explanationKey: The executive branch has many parts. Name one.
facts: The executive branch includes the President, the Cabinet and federal departments and agencies.
The Cabinet is a group of leaders who advise the President.

newWords.meaning: the group of top leaders who advise the President

story.say: The executive branch has many parts.

help.simpler: The executive branch is bigger than just the President.
help.example: It has the President, the Cabinet and many departments and agencies.
help.why: The test asks you to name one part of the executive branch.

story.say: It includes the President, the Cabinet, and federal departments and agencies.

help.simpler: These are the main parts of the executive branch.
help.example: The Department of Education and the Department of Agriculture are two federal departments.
help.why: “President,” “Cabinet” and “federal departments and agencies” are all answers on the test.

story.say: The Cabinet is a group of leaders who advise the President.

help.simpler: The Cabinet gives the President advice.
help.example: “Advise” means to give ideas and help someone decide.
help.why: The test asks what the Cabinet does. The answer: it advises the President.

story.say: The Cabinet helps the President make decisions.

help.simpler: Cabinet members share what they know, and the President decides.
help.example: This picture shows President Lincoln meeting with his Cabinet in 1862.
help.why: Remember: the Cabinet advises the President.

check.prompt: What does the President’s Cabinet do?

facts: Each Cabinet member leads one part of the executive branch.
Two Cabinet-level positions are the Secretary of State and the Attorney General.

newWords.meaning: the leader of one federal department
the top lawyer of the federal government

story.say: Each Cabinet member leads one part of the executive branch.

help.simpler: Every Cabinet member is in charge of one department.
help.example: The Secretary of Education leads the Department of Education.
help.why: Their job titles are the answers to the test question about Cabinet positions.

story.say: Two Cabinet-level positions are the Secretary of State and the Attorney General.

help.simpler: Secretary of State and Attorney General are two jobs in the Cabinet.
help.example: The Secretary of State works with other countries. The Attorney General leads the Department of Justice.
help.why: The test asks you to name two Cabinet-level positions.

check.statement: The Attorney General is a Cabinet-level position.

story.say: Say them together: the Secretary of State and the Attorney General.

help.simpler: Practice saying the two titles out loud.
help.example: Officer: “Name two Cabinet-level positions.” You: “Secretary of State and Attorney General.”
help.why: Saying them out loud helps you remember them on the day.

check.prompt: Which one is a Cabinet-level position?

help.simpler: Leaders change over time, so the app checks an official list.
help.example: There is an election for President every four years.
